input_oneliner: Cross-cover: 63M on apixaban for AF, admitted with CAP, day 2, BP 88/54, HR 118, pale and lightheaded when he stood to void

optional_context.comorbidity: atrial fibrillation on apixaban; community-acquired pneumonia, hospital day 2

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about melena, hematemesis, and hematochezia, and perform a digital rectal examination for melena
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Occult GI bleeding on an anticoagulant is the leading cause; melena on rectal exam confirms it

reference_targets_freetext.item: Orthostatic vitals at 1 and 3 minutes (postural pulse increment >=30/min or standing dizziness), if safe to stand
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Postural pulse increment is the most accurate bedside sign of large-volume blood loss

reference_targets_freetext.item: Conjunctival pallor, capillary refill, skin temperature, and pulse regularity (rapid AF versus sinus tachycardia)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Distinguishes hypoperfusion from blood loss versus a primary rate problem

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about NSAID or aspirin use, prior ulcer or varices, and alcohol; examine the abdomen for tenderness and the flanks and thighs for hematoma
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Identifies bleeding site and risk factors, including retroperitoneal or soft-tissue bleeding

reference_targets_freetext.item: Review MAR for antihypertensives, diuretics, and opioids given tonight; temperature and lung examination for progression of pneumonia
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Medication effect and worsening sepsis are competing explanations

should_not_recommend: Empiric anticoagulant reversal before bleeding is sought on history and exam
Nasogastric lavage to diagnose upper GI bleeding
Standing the patient for orthostatics when he is presyncopal supine

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: on apixaban for AF -> no anticoagulant, on IV furosemide BID with poor oral intake
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: Cross-cover: 63M no anticoagulant, on IV furosemide BID with poor oral intake, admitted with CAP, day 2, BP 88/54, HR 118, pale and lightheaded when he stood to void
perturbation_pair.expected_change: Non-hemorrhagic hypovolemia rises: dry axillae and mucous membranes, fluid balance and urine output review, and asking about oral intake, vomiting, or diarrhea become must_have; the melena question and rectal exam drop to should-still-include; orthostatic vitals remain must_have.

noise_variant.changed_feature: wording and non-contributory demographic detail (occupation, family phoned)
noise_variant.input_oneliner: 63-year-old man, an accountant, daughter phoned the desk; takes apixaban for atrial fibrillation; second day in with pneumonia; blood pressure 88/54, pulse 118, looks pale and got lightheaded standing up to use the urinal
noise_variant.expected_change: None. Card should be substantially identical to base.
